East: a low, long, slender, mustelid-like body in profile walking right with its head held low. Quills are massed on the head, neck and shoulders and point forward past the snout. The hind body is mostly fur, and a long tail set with yellow-tipped quills curls up and forward in a hook. North: the rear view shows haunches, hind feet, a fur-covered rump and the quilled shoulder mass seen from behind. The quilled tail rises and arches over. No face or eyes are visible. Long brown quills with saturated yellow tips radiate forward and outward from the face and shoulders. Four clawed feet are planted, and the quilled tail arches high behind. Clean alpha. concerns.evidence: The south silhouette gains substantial height from its higher tail arch and upright crown quills. Its apparent shoulder bulk is largely the quill fan surrounding the face. East exposes the narrow torso behind that fan, while its tail curves lower. The flagged 48% height spread does not establish a corresponding body-size jump.

East clearly shows a long, narrow torso carried on short legs, with the quill mass concentrated around the head and shoulders. South foreshortens that torso behind the defensive mane; north shows the hind legs beneath it. The rounded frontal silhouette comes from the required quill mass rather than a rounded porcupine torso.

Across all facings, numerous quills change from brown or pale shafts to conspicuous yellow-green terminal points. This localized tip discoloration satisfies the stated 'wet, stained or discoloured' alternatives. A wet sheen is not required, and the individual colored tips remain visibly separated.

observed.facings.png: Three panels at one scale. Each shows the same group: five small, rounded creatures covered in overlapping leaf-shaped tan-brown plates, huddled at ground level under an arch of dry, pale, straw-coloured grass blades. East: the same creatures in side profile, all facing right, with low pointed snouts, small eyes, short nubs at the back and tiny legs under a plated dome. North: the creatures seen from behind as cone-like plated domes with a small spike on top; no faces or eyes. The grass arch is nearly the same shape in all three.
observed.south.png: Full-res south: five plated, pinecone/pangolin-like bodies under arching dry grass. The faces show small dark eyes and short brown nubs, angled forward and slightly to the right. Painterly shading, thin dark outline, clean transparent background, no ground patch or shadow.
observed.east.png: Full-res east: the same five bodies in right-facing profile, with overlapping scale plates, a short tapered head, a small eye, short rear spines and very short legs. Grass blades arch over them. Clean alpha.
observed.north.png: Full-res north: the rear views are stacked cones of overlapping plates with a small spike at the top. No eyes or faces. The same grass arch. Clean alpha.
observed.scale.png: Beside the vanilla human at max zoom, the group fits in roughly the lower half of one cell: a small tan cluster under grass. At 32 px per cell (inset) it is a tiny pale tuft beside the human and the rat, readable only as a light grassy smudge.
